card.name: Just before the word anticoagulant
card.fires_on: Words and word parts right before an expected "anticoagulant" or "anticoagulation" in heparin, warfarin and apixaban labels. It also fires on dose numbers and "of" in anticoagulant dosing text.

modes.label: Leading into anticoagulant
modes.description: An adjective or the start of the word, where "anticoagulant" or "anticoagulation" comes next.
modes.example: To ensure<< continuous>> anticoagulation when converting from H

modes.label: Inside anticoagulant drug names
modes.description: The middle of a blood-thinner name such as apixaban.
modes.example: reduces blood levels of ap<<ix>>aban: Avoid concomitant use.

modes.label: Dose figures in anticoagulant text
modes.description: A digit, space or "of" in a unit or duration phrase in heparin or warfarin dosing.
modes.example: at a dose of 1 mg protamine for every 100 anti-Xa units<< of>> FRAGMIN given.

card.writes: It promotes pieces such as ant, plate, throm and fibr, which start clotting-related words.
card.plain: It lights up when the text is about to say anticoagulant or another clotting-related term in blood-thinner labels.
